---
title: "Record schema"
---

The output contract: one schema-1 record per target per pass, streaming
JSONL. The field lists below are the encoders' contract — pinned by the
goldens in the test tree, drift-checked against the published
[machine-readable schema](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/blob/main/docs/schema-v1.json)
in CI. Full prose context:
[the spec §5.7](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/blob/main/docs/spec.md#57-output-dialect-and-machine-format).

## Block order

``` {mermaid}
flowchart LR
  T[target] --> H[handshake] --> Q[quic] --> C[cert] --> P[pq] --> D["deep (deep mode)"] --> E[error]
```

| Block | Fields |
|---|---|
| `target` | `input`, `host`, `ip`, `port`, `ptr`, `sni_used` |
| `handshake` | `negotiated` (group id), `group_name`, `group_class`, `suite`, `version`, `alpn_neg` |
| `quic` | `attempted`, `state` (negotiated · handshaked · refused · mismatch · skipped · udp_blocked), `negotiated`, `group_name`, `group_class`, `discovered{alt_svc_h3, h3_direct}` |
| `cert` | `sig_alg`, `sig_pq`, `key_alg`, `key_pq`, `dual` |
| `pq` | `score` (0–100), `label` (`pq-ready` ≥ 80, `pq-ready-hybrid` ≥ 60, `pq-partial` ≥ 40, `pq-missing` ≥ 1), `hndl`, `summary` |
| `deep` | deep mode only: `mode`, `attempted`, `ok`, `rejected`, `findings[]{probe, result, detail}` |
| `error` | the per-target error string |

## The fast record (captured on google.com)

```bash
$ pqscan -u google.com -jsonl
```

```json
{"schema":1,"mode":"fast","target":{"input":"google.com","host":"google.com","ip":"","port":443,"ptr":"","sni_used":""},"handshake":{"negotiated":4588,"group_name":"X25519MLKEM768","group_class":"pq_hybrid","suite":"TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256","version":"tls-1.3","alpn_neg":"h2"},"quic":{"attempted":true,"state":"negotiated","negotiated":4588,"group_name":"X25519MLKEM768","group_class":"pq_hybrid","discovered":{"alt_svc_h3":true,"h3_direct":true}},"cert":{"sig_alg":"sha256WithRSAEncryption","sig_pq":false,"key_alg":"ECDSA","key_pq":false,"dual":false},"pq":{"score":40,"label":"pq-partial","hndl":false,"summary":"negotiated_pq_hybrid(+40)"},"error":""}
```

## The CSV projection

25 columns, header first; the order below is the contract:

```text
target,host,port,ptr,sni,negotiated,group_name,group_class,suite,version,alpn,quic_state,quic_group,udp_blocked,cert_sig_alg,cert_sig_pq,cert_key_alg,cert_key_pq,cert_dual,pq_score,pq_label,pq_hndl,pq_summary,error,ts
```

## Exit codes

| code | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | scan completed (per-target errors are records, not failures) |
| 1 | runtime error (engine/system) |
| 2 | flag-parse error |
| 64 | EX_USAGE: no targets to scan |
| 130 | interrupted (drains before exit; WAL retained) |

Consumption recipes (jq views, the estate calendar, the adapters) live on
the Recipes page; the human-readable man-format flag reference is USAGE.

## How it stays honest

- The **goldens** (`tests/goldens/record.*`) pin the byte-shape; a contract
  change = a visible golden diff in review.
- The **schema-sync check** regenerates
  [`docs/schema-v1.json`](https://github.com/shsingh/pqscan/blob/main/docs/schema-v1.json)
  from the goldens and requires byte equality — the published schema cannot
  drift from what the binary emits.
- The **usage-drift gate** keeps USAGE.md honest against the flags.
